title: SQL Generator Evaluation Report
purpose: Evaluate whether the SQL generator correctly translates the logical plan into SQL.

results.analysis: Correct count intent, but differs from expected expression.

results.expected: SELECT product_id, category, popularity_score FROM products ORDER BY popularity_score DESC LIMIT 5;
results.actual: SELECT product_id, category, price, margin_percentage, popularity_score FROM products ORDER BY popularity_score DESC LIMIT 5;
results.analysis: Correct ranking, but adds unnecessary columns.
Missing FROM transactions, making the SQL invalid.

results.expected: SELECT country, COUNT(customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY customer_count DESC LIMIT 1;
results.actual: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY customer_count DESC LIMIT 1;
results.analysis: Correct core logic, but uses COUNT(*) instead of COUNT(customer_id).

results.expected: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(transaction_id) AS order_count FROM transactions GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(transaction_id) > 3;
results.actual: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM transactions GROUP BY customer_id HAVING transaction_count > 3;
results.analysis: Correct grouping/filtering, but changes the count expression and alias.

results.expected: SELECT AVG(b.avg_session_time) FROM customers c JOIN behaviors b ON c.customer_id = b.customer_id WHERE c.loyalty_score > 0.8;
results.actual: SELECT AVG(behaviors.avg_session_time) AS avg_session_time_for_high_loyalty_customers FROM customers INNER JOIN behaviors ON customers.customer_id = behaviors.customer_id WHERE customers.loyalty_score >= (SELECT MIN(c.loyalty_score) FROM customers c);
results.analysis: Changes the requested loyalty_score > 0.8 condition into unrelated logic.

results.expected: SELECT DISTINCT p.product_id, p.category FROM products p JOIN transactions t ON p.product_id = t.product_id WHERE t.device_type = 'mobile';
results.actual: SELECT products.product_id, products.category, products.price FROM transactions JOIN products ON transactions.product_id = products.product_id WHERE transactions.device_type = 'mobile';
results.analysis: Correct join/filter, but adds price and omits DISTINCT.
Generates destructive SQL instead of rejecting it.

analysis.summary: The generator now produces cleaner SQL, but does not consistently preserve the intended logic.
strengths: Mostly returns a single SQL statement.
Several queries have the correct core logic.
Previous output-format problem is largely improved.
analysis.boundary: The generator should translate the logical plan into SQL, not invent or change requirements.

conclusion: Baseline: 0% full-pass and 62.5% partial-or-better. Future evaluation should focus on faithful translation of a correct plan.
